title: Ream the burr off a freshly cut copper tube
instruction: Remove the burr from inside the freshly cut copper tube's end with the hand reamer, without over-chamfering the thin wall, then stand the tube back in its rack and put the reamer down.
context: Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters (O*NET 47-2152.00, about 0.5 million employed in the US) and HVAC mechanics and installers (49-9021.00, about 0.4 million) cut copper tube all day, and every cut leaves a burr round the inside of the end. Reaming it off is a required step before a joint is made (the fitting makers and ASTM B828 call for it): a left burr makes turbulence and erosion in the line, and a reamer run too long chamfers the thin wall. The tube is held upright in one hand while the other turns the reamer, and since the wrist does not turn far the hand lets go and re-grips between strokes.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A tube rack (fixed: a 90 x 90 x 4 mm plate with a 27 mm bore through a 20 mm high wall, with a 7 mm 45 degree lead-in) stands at x 0.27, y -0.05. A freshly cut piece of 22 x 0.9 mm copper tube (EN 1057 R250: 22 mm outside, 20.2 mm bore, 100 mm long, 0.053 kg, free; one fresh coupon from the batch in reset_notes) stands in it, open end up, with a 0.40 +/-0.05 mm burr round the inside of the end. A reamer rest (fixed: a 90 x 90 x 6 mm plate with an 18 mm bore through an 18 mm high wall, 5 mm lead-in) stands at x 0.22, y -0.20; the reamer (free: an inner-outer deburring reamer with a conical blade 8 mm at the tip and 26 mm across 14 mm up, a 45 mm cutting cup and a 30 mm handle, 72 mm long, 0.090 kg) stands in it, cone down.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged as things stand at the end. (1) The reamer's blade was engaged in the burr of the tube while a gripper held it: the cone's real 4-13 mm edge (slope 9/14) at least 0.05 mm inside the 0.40 mm burr's 9.70 mm inner edge, so the tip is 8.944-9.800 mm below the rim, within 3 mm of the bore's axis and 8 degrees of its line; at 6 mm the 7.857 mm edge is 1.843 mm clear of the burr, contact is 0 N and nothing counts. (2) Every one of 12 sectors of the bore has had at least one blade pass (the burr at least half removed all round). (3) Every sector has had two passes (burr removed all round) and no sector's rim has been chamfered past 0.5 mm. (4) With step 3: the tube stands in its rack (its lower end within 4 mm of the bore's axis and of its seat, leaning less than 20 degrees), the reamer's cone is out of the bore, no gripper holds either part and no pad is within 3 cm of either. A blade pass counts only while the reamer turns clockwise, the blade is engaged in the burr (0.05-0.60 mm bite, 13.2 N per blade at the 0.08 N m cut torque; at least 5 N), a gripper holds the tube; turning back, or turning in any other state, cuts nothing. Each pass over a sector with its burr gone chamfers its rim by 0.2 mm, so turning on past the burr thins the wall: past 0.5 mm steps 3 and 4 are lost for good (score at most 0.4). Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once all four steps have held together, without a break, for 1 s, with the tube and reamer within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where they were when that second began; any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8. Scoring 0 for the whole run: the tube or the reamer off the table, or the tube dropped or knocked over (tipped more than 60 degrees). Real trial: a 10x loupe or scaled photo and 19.7/20.0 mm go plugs; step 2 every sector's lip <=0.20 mm and the 19.7 mm plug enters 30 mm; step 3 no lip visible at 10x, 20.0 mm plug enters 30 mm, end-face bevel <=0.50 mm (0.30-0.50 mm normal; >0.50 mm over-ream); step 4 tube in rack, reamer in rest, nothing held or within 30 mm.
reset_notes: One fresh 22 x 0.9 x 100 mm coupon per trial, inner lip 0.40 +/-0.05 mm: cut with a wheel-type tube cutter (RIDGID 151/E-3469 or equivalent, 1/16 turn feed per revolution), do not ream; measure at 12 points with a 10x loupe and 0.1 mm reticle and keep 0.35-0.45 mm (or use machined coupons to the same drawing). Stand it in the rack, open end up; reamer cone-down in its rest; nothing held. Full method and citations: README 'Reset and the 0.40 mm burr coupon'.
fidelity: Burr/chamfer are declared effects, not simulated metal: 12 sectors, two blades, 0.2 mm per pass. A pass needs real blade contact: the cone's 4-13 mm edge (slope 9/14) must bite 0.05-0.60 mm into the 0.40 mm burr ring (tip 8.944-9.800 mm below the rim); at 6 mm the edge is 1.843 mm clear, contact 0 N, nothing counts. The cut's 0.08 N m torque is an equal/opposite pair (13.2 N per blade at mu 0.30). 100 mm offcut; rigid parts at true size; rack is the authors' bench fixture.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, step limit); demo: 1.0 at step 1027 on Isaac (media M-C7YEFJ); revised MuJoCo stand-in: 1.0 at step 1017 (50.9 s).
